judge_panel.reason: The paper provides constraint (9) stating 'y_i ≤ Σ_{j∈V_RSU} 𝕀{path exists from i to j}' but never provides a constraint that forces y_i = 1 only when CAV i actually has an active outgoing edge (x_ij = 1 for some j) or ensures y_i = 0 when no such edge exists. The formulation is incomplete as presented — the connectivity variable y_i is not explicitly linked to the binary edge-activation variables x_ij through a tying constraint, leaving the MILP formulation under-specified as written.

Section III-C does include a constraint tying connectivity to the selected topology: "yi ≤ Σ_{j∈VRSU} I{path exists from i to j}, ∀i ∈ VCAV" (Eq. 9). If no path to any RSU exists, the right-hand side is 0, which forces "yi = 0," so the reviewer's claim that no such constraint exists is factually incorrect.

While Equation (9) presents a conceptual constraint (`y_i \leq \sum_{j \in V_{RSU}} \mathbb{I}\{\text{path exists from } i \text{ to } j\}`), it is an indicator function that is not mathematically linked to the decision variables `x_{ij}` or flows, leaving the objective function disconnected from the routing decisions in the MILP.

judge_panel.reason: Section V-G states 'L2O improves 1-hop connectivity in more than 97% of the evaluated snapshots,' which is ambiguous at best and misleading at worst, since the paper's premise is multi-hop relay selection beyond single-hop V2I. The paper does not clarify whether this means L2O exceeds the single-hop baseline, the greedy baseline, or something else, and the phrase 'improves 1-hop connectivity' contradicts the multi-hop framing of the entire paper.

Section V-G states, "Overall, across all regimes, L2O improves 1-hop connectivity in more than 97% of the evaluated snapshots," but elsewhere the paper defines the method as a multi-hop relay selector and defines connectivity as "single- or multi-hop paths" with gain measured relative to "a single-hop V2I baseline" (Section V-B). As written, the sentence is technically inconsistent/misleading because L2O does not itself change the 1-hop baseline.

The paper states in Section V-G that "L2O improves 1-hop connectivity in more than 97% of the evaluated snapshots, confirming that learning-based relay selection consistently outperforms local greedy heuristics." This sentence is ambiguous as it conflates exceeding the 1-hop baseline with outperforming the greedy heuristic, while technically L2O bypasses rather than modifies 1-hop connectivity.
